llm_narrative: Across the 500 evaluation tasks the qwen3.5_35b_output model achieved a mean claim‑coverage of only 0.2089 and a median of 0, with just 10.4 % of instances reaching the 75 % coverage threshold; 103 runs (20.6 %) produced empty answers despite zero infra errors. Failure diagnostics covered 470 tasks (94 % of the sample), and tool‑related breakdowns dominated: 326 failures (69.4 % of all failures) were tied to tool calls, of which wrong‑tool selection accounted for 160 cases and error‑recovery lapses for another 130, while purely cognitive errors comprised only 144 instances (30.6 %). The model’s inability to select the correct MCP endpoint and to recover from “unknown tool” or malformed‑call responses is the primary driver of low coverage, whereas reasoning deficits play a secondary role. A concrete remediation is to augment the pre‑call validation layer with a lookup of available tool signatures and an automated fallback strategy that retries using alternative, semantically equivalent tools when the first call fails. This failure profile distinguishes qwen3.5_35b_output from other models by its disproportionately high incidence of wrong‑tool and unrecovered tool errors—issues that manifest as early termination or empty outputs rather than reasoning mistakes.
